recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-7859 unless the Patient Care work group wants to reopen the broader recordedDate wording established by later Jira decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-7859 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Patient Care change request asking that Condition.dateAsserted stop overlapping onset and instead represent the date the Condition statement was documented, with the element renamed to recordedDate.
initial_application: Historical commit c6b154ca1b explicitly cited #7615, #7855, and #7859, renamed Condition.dateAsserted to Condition.dateRecorded in the then-current Condition spreadsheet and examples, and changed the wording from first detected/suspected to a documented/record-created date.
additional_context: Later source history renamed the element through Condition.assertedDate to the current Condition.recordedDate, with fhir.ini preserving those rename chains. Subsequent Condition issues and commits, including GF#14643/GF#17285 and J#27808/J#34392/J#34394, refined the current element to say the record was created/first recorded and clarified preservation and recorder semantics. No relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that conflicts with the Jira/source/history conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists Condition as an active resource, and source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml currently defines Condition.recordedDate with short text 'Date condition was first recorded' and a definition that it represents when the particular Condition record was created in the system.
